p: of blood that emerges from two corpses,
“Neither shall he go in to any dead bodies”
A nazirite shaves for … these … ritual impurity:
A nazirite shaves for having become impure from these following sources of ritual impurity:
a limb from a corpse or for … a limb … from a living … upon … which there is a fitting … flesh; … and for
a limb from a corpse or for impurity imparted by a limb severed from a living person, upon either of which there is a fitting quantity of flesh; and for
by coming into contact with them; … and for … carrying them;
by coming into contact with them; and for becoming impure by carrying them;
for a bone that is a barley-grain-bulk,
coming into contact with it and by carrying it.

w.8: that is a barley grain bulk
w.10: coming into contact with it … by carrying it

p: on the third and on the seventh
only after he becomes pure and brings his offerings.
Rabbi Yehuda said to his students:
Do not let the students of Rabbi Meir enter here,
because they are vexatious and they do not come to study Torah,
but they come to overwhelm me with … halakhot. … Sumakhos, … forced his way and entered
but they come to overwhelm me with their halakhot. Nevertheless, Sumakhos, a student of Rabbi Meir, forced his way and entered

w.28: they come to overwhelm me … Sumakhos … forced his way

p: Rabbi Meir taught me like this:
A nazirite shaves for … these … ritual impurity:
A nazirite shaves for becoming impure from these following sources of ritual impurity:
Rabbi Yehuda grew angry and said to … Didn’t I say to you like this:
Rabbi Yehuda grew angry and said to his disciples: Didn’t I say to you like this:
Do not let the students of Rabbi Meir enter here because they are vexatious? … must shave for
Do not let the students of Rabbi Meir enter here because they are vexatious? He explained his annoyance. The clause: For a corpse, is unnecessary, as, if a nazirite must shave for
not all the more so … for … corpse?
not all the more so that he must shave for impurity imparted by an entire corpse?
